newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia president greets Timor Nobel winner Belo.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia president greets Timor Nobel winner Belo.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto on Tuesday greeted 1996 Nobel Peace Prize winner Bishop Carlos Belo during a ceremony in the East Timor capital but appeared not to exchange any words, witnesses said.

Suharto made a whirlwind tour to the former Portuguese colony attending a ceremony at the seaside office of the territory's governor where he inaugarated a number of public works projects in a visit of a little over three hours.
Belo, along with self-exiled East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for being an "indefatigable" supporter of peace through dialogue.
"Suharto publicly shook hands with Belo twice but said nothing," a witness said.
During the signing ceremony, Belo sat next to Indonesian Armed Forces chief General Feisal Tanjung who appeared to congratulate Belo, the witness said.

Belo, East Timor's Catholic bishop, was later scheduled to join Suharto on a short helicopter ride during which the president's party were to view a 27-metre (90-foot) high statue of Jesus Christ outside Dili as well as a number of road and bridge projects.
